title: Your Healthcare Operations Platform: Intake and Document Triage First

sections.label: 1 - INTAKE SUPPORT AND DOCUMENT TRIAGE
sections.note: Your part 1, intake support and document triage; its internal task routing lands in section 4. Staff send an item from the portal, their role is checked and patient identifiers are masked before any model sees it.

sections.label: 2 - RAG OVER YOUR POLICIES, SOPS, FORMS AND SERVICE GUIDELINES
sections.note: Your part 2, and your question on keeping the AI useful as the knowledge base grows: each item is matched only against the active version of your own documents, filtered by service line and by what the staff role may see. When an admin edits a document, KB 1 to KB 4 re-index it and retire the old version, so no answer cites an outdated SOP; items with no matching passage are logged as gaps, so admins see what to write next.

sections.label: 3 - CLAUDE FIRST, OPENAI AS FALLBACK, CLEAR BOUNDARIES
sections.note: Your part 3: Claude triages from the matched passages only, cites them and never makes a clinical call. If Claude fails, OpenAI runs the same rules; anything unsure, uncited or clinical goes to a person.

sections.label: 4 - ROUTE THE TASK OR SEND IT TO THE REVIEW QUEUE
sections.note: Your parts 4 and 5: the API call into your internal tools, and the review queue behind your admin screen. Confident, cited items become a task in the right queue; everything else waits for staff to approve, edit or reject it.

sections.label: 5 - AUDIT TRAIL, PERMISSIONS AND THE STAFF SCREEN
sections.note: Your parts 6 and 7: logging, permissions and audit trail, then the staff web interface. Permissions are checked at steps 2 and 3 and filter retrieval at step 6; every action, that check included, gets its own append-only audit row with who, what, which sources and which model, and the staff screen shows status, owner, next steps and sources in plain words. Every later workflow reuses sections 2 to 5 as they are, so new workflows can be added without rebuilding the entire system.

sections.label: 6 - IF ANY STEP FAILS
sections.note: The item is held for manual handling, the failure is logged, and the admin screen is flagged with no patient details in the alert, so nothing sits silently.

nodes.label: 1 - New Intake Item or Document From the Staff Portal
2 - Look Up the Staff Role, Mark the Item In Progress

params.query:
WITH in_progress AS (
  UPDATE intake_items
  SET status = 'processing', execution_id = $3, updated_at = now()
  WHERE item_id = $2
  RETURNING item_id
)
SELECT role, can_submit_intake, service_lines
FROM staff_users
WHERE portal_user_id = $1 AND active = true
LIMIT 1;

nodes.label: 4 - Mask Patient Identifiers Before Any Model Sees Them
nodes.notes: The name on file, dates, phone numbers, emails, SSNs and member IDs are masked before any model call. This cuts what a model sees but is not de-identification, so real patient data waits for your BAAs.

nodes.label: 5 - OpenAI: Turn the Masked Text Into a Search Vector
6 - Supabase: Find the Matching Policy, SOP and Form Passages

params.query:
SELECT COALESCE(json_agg(t ORDER BY t.similarity DESC), '[]'::json) AS passages,
       COALESCE(MAX(t.similarity), 0) AS top_similarity
FROM (
  SELECT chunk_id, doc_id, doc_title, doc_type, version, section_heading, content,
         1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) AS similarity
  FROM kb_chunks
  WHERE status = 'active'
    AND (service_line = $2 OR service_line = 'all')
    AND $3 = ANY (visible_to_roles)
  ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector
  LIMIT 6
) t;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ JSON.stringify($json.data[0].embedding), $('4 - Mask Patient Identifiers Before Any Model Sees Them').item.json.service_line, $('4 - Mask Patient Identifiers Before Any Model Sees Them').item.json.staff_role ] }}

nodes.label: 7 - Found a Passage That Covers This Item?
KB 1 - Admin Saves or Edits a Policy, SOP, Form or Guideline
KB 2 - Split Into Passages Tagged With Doc, Version, Section
KB 3 - OpenAI: Embed Every Passage in One Call
KB 4 - Supabase: Store the New Version, Retire the Old One

params.query:
WITH retired AS (
  UPDATE kb_chunks SET status = 'retired', retired_at = now()
  WHERE doc_id = $1 AND status = 'active'
  RETURNING chunk_id
), logged AS (
  INSERT INTO audit_log (staff_user_id, execution_id, action, outcome, detail, created_at)
  VALUES ($7, $8, 'kb_document_reindexed', 'active', $1 || ' now v' || $5, now())
)
INSERT INTO kb_chunks (chunk_id, doc_id, doc_title, doc_type, service_line, visible_to_roles, version, section_heading, content, embedding, status, created_at)
SELECT p.chunk_id, $1, $2, $3, $4, $6::text[], $5, p.section_heading, p.content, e.embedding::vector, 'active', now()
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($9::jsonb) AS p(idx int, chunk_id text, section_heading text, content text)
JOIN jsonb_to_recordset($10::jsonb) AS e("index" int, embedding text) ON e."index" = p.idx
RETURNING chunk_id, version;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ (() => { const d = $('KB 1 - Admin Saves or Edits a Policy, SOP, Form or Guideline').item.json.body; return [d.doc_id, d.doc_title, d.doc_type, d.service_line || 'all', String(d.version), '{' + (d.visible_to_roles || []).join(',') + '}', d.edited_by, $execution.id, JSON.stringify($('KB 2 - Split Into Passages Tagged With Doc, Version, Section').item.json.passages), JSON.stringify($json.data)]; })() }}

nodes.label: 8 - Claude Triages Using Only Your Documents
nodes.notes: No source, no answer: it cites your documents or hands the item to a person.

params.system_message: You triage administrative intake items for a healthcare services business. You support office staff with paperwork; you do not replace clinical judgment. Hard boundaries: never diagnose, never assess symptoms, never suggest treatment or medication, and never judge how urgent care is. If the item describes symptoms, asks a clinical question or suggests a patient's health may be at risk, set category to clinical_question and needs_human to true, write one neutral line in summary_for_staff and stop. Use only the SOURCES passages you are given. Every next step must be supported by a passage you cite by chunk_id. If the sources do not cover the item, or two queues fit equally well, set needs_human to true and say why in reason. Never invent a policy, form name, deadline, fee, phone number or queue. Patient identifiers are masked as [NAME], [DATE], [PHONE], [EMAIL], [SSN] and [MEMBER_ID]; never guess or restore them, and do not repeat them in your summary. owner_queue must be exactly one of the ALLOWED QUEUES. priority is administrative only: time_sensitive when the document states a deadline, otherwise routine. confidence is your honest probability, 0 to 1, that category and owner_queue are right given the sources; stay below 0.8 when the document is partial, unreadable or contradicts the sources. Return only the requested fields as JSON.

nodes.label: 14 - Update the Staff Screen: Status, Owner, Sources

params.query:
UPDATE intake_items
SET status = $2, owner_queue = $3, staff_summary = $4, next_steps = $5::jsonb,
    cited_sources = $6::jsonb, ai_model = $7, ai_confidence = $8, task_ref = $9, updated_at = now()
WHERE item_id = $1
RETURNING item_id, status, owner_queue, staff_summary, next_steps, cited_sources, ai_model, ai_confidence, task_ref, updated_at;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ (() => { const s = $('12 - Build One Audit Row per Action Taken').first().json.screen; return [s.item_id, s.status, s.owner_queue, s.staff_summary, JSON.stringify(s.next_steps || []), JSON.stringify(s.cited_sources || []), s.ai_model, s.ai_confidence, s.task_ref || null]; })() }}

nodes.label: 15 - Any Step Fails, Anywhere
16 - Log It and Flag the Admin Screen, No Patient Details

params.query:
WITH held AS (
  UPDATE intake_items SET status = 'manual_handling', updated_at = now()
  WHERE execution_id = $1
  RETURNING item_id
), logged AS (
  INSERT INTO audit_log (item_id, execution_id, action, outcome, detail, created_at)
  SELECT item_id, $1, 'workflow_failed', 'manual_handling', 'stopped at ' || $2, now() FROM held
)
INSERT INTO admin_alerts (execution_id, failed_step, message, created_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, 'Intake triage stopped at ' || $2 || '. The item is held for manual handling; details are in the n8n execution log.', now())
RETURNING id, failed_step;
